name: wazuh-ai-ops: Enrichment/Triage TEST HARNESS (mirrors fixture values, not live endpoints)
notes: Test harness for enrichment-triage.n8n.json's assembly and dashboard-payload logic. It does NOT call the four enrichment HTTP endpoints in the main workflow -- 'Load Fixture Data' mirrors the mock_enrichment_responses values from workflows/fixtures/enrichment-triage.fixture.json by hand (not read from the file at runtime, to avoid a filesystem-path dependency that would vary across n8n installs; if you self-host and prefer a single source of truth, swap that node for a 'Read/Write Files from Disk' + JSON-parse pair pointed at the fixture file). Keep the two in sync manually when either changes. The structural assertions in 'Run Assertions' (disposition/disposed_by/status/travel_status) run regardless of the LLM step. The LLM call itself still needs a real self-hosted inference endpoint behind 'LLM: Generate Triage Brief (Test)' to execute end-to-end -- without one, use n8n's 'Pin Data' feature on that node to stub a response and exercise the assertions in isolation. Run 'Positive Case' and 'Negative Case' separately from their own manual triggers.

nodes.name: Load Fixture Data
nodes.notes: This is the node that makes the fixture executable: it replaces the four live 'Enrich: *' HTTP nodes from the main workflow with the same mock data the fixture file specifies.

Anything about whether the model 'understood' the negative case correctly is language-dependent and is surfaced here for a human to read, not asserted as pass/fail -- the fixture's own criteria list makes the same distinction.
